papers.title: ProtAgents: protein discovery via large language model multi-agent collaborations combining physics and machine learning
papers.version: arXiv:2402.04268v1 (27 January 2024); journal publication verified separately
papers.summary: Prescribed agent roles connect protein generation, folding, mechanics prediction and normal-mode calculations.

representation.rationale: Tool integration retains supplied protein descriptors.

transfer.rationale: Familiar computational techniques combined within protein analysis.

formal.rationale: Function schemas structure calls; no composition guarantee established.

dynamics.rationale: Vibrations and unfolding properties are central analyzed outcomes.

organization.rationale: Planner, Assistant, Critic and manager have prescribed roles.

explanation.rationale: Examples demonstrate orchestration more than discriminating mechanisms.

validation.rationale: Executed ANM calculations accompany learned property predictions.

robustness.rationale: Illustrative tasks expose failures; broad comparative testing unreviewed.

surprise.observation: The Critic repairs malformed data and identifies a failed structural conditioning case.
surprise.interpretation: Useful scientific workflow supervision extends beyond generating sequences.
surprise.boundary: Successful conversations do not establish general autonomous reliability.

detail.observation: ProteinForceGPT is used only for forward predictions; normal modes use ANM.
detail.consequence: Computed modes and predicted unfolding forces carry different evidential weight.

notRead: Journal full text blocked; external supplements, code and raw outputs not inspected.

papers.title: AtomAgents: Alloy design and discovery through physics-aware multi-modal multi-agent artificial intelligence
papers.status: Author preprint assessed; published subsequently in PNAS (2025)
papers.summary: Prescribed agents plan alloy calculations and evaluate hypotheses with atomistic simulations.

representation.rationale: Automates established alloy variables and simulation workflows.

transfer.rationale: Multimodal integration remains within alloy mechanics.

formal.rationale: Fracture calculation imposes explicit elasticity-theory relations.

dynamics.rationale: Transition paths inform static barriers and toughness estimates.

organization.rationale: Planner/Critic and a manager coordinate prescribed roles.

explanation.rationale: NbMo simulations quantify an energy-variation/Peierls-barrier relationship.

validation.rationale: LAMMPS and NEB calculations test alloy hypotheses.

robustness.rationale: Potential comparisons and configuration sampling; broader generality remains open.

surprise.observation: A generated barrier-correlation hypothesis is followed by NEB calculations.
surprise.interpretation: The contribution includes executing a test, beyond proposing materials.
surprise.boundary: One simulated alloy system does not establish universal design laws.

detail.observation: LAMMPS scripts are human-authored; core-image interpretation needs labeled examples.
detail.consequence: Autonomy depends on prepared tools and task-specific contextual support.

notRead: External supporting figures, raw simulations and PNAS revision not inspected.

papers.title: Agentic End-to-End De Novo Protein Design for Tailored Dynamics Using a Language Diffusion Model
papers.status: Author preprint assessed; peer-reviewed Matter publication verified (2026)
papers.summary: Protein sequences are generated for prescribed residue-wise vibrational amplitudes, then screened by a predictor.

representation.rationale: Dynamics becomes an inverse-design descriptor alongside sequence and structure.

transfer.rationale: Language diffusion and mechanics combine within protein design.

formal.rationale: Coordinate-invariant amplitude descriptor constrains a limited component.

dynamics.rationale: Inverse design targets detailed normal-mode amplitude profiles.

organization.rationale: Designer and predictor have fixed specialized coordination.

explanation.rationale: Secondary-structure confinement correlates with designed local amplitudes.

validation.rationale: Folded designs undergo force-field normal-mode calculations.

robustness.rationale: Held-out random split and predictor-selection comparisons; cluster separation unestablished.

surprise.observation: Different generated folds can satisfy similar vibrational profiles.
surprise.interpretation: A family of motions can organize design alternatives.
surprise.boundary: Mode matching does not demonstrate enzymatic function or cellular dynamics.

detail.observation: Target is only the first nontrivial mode’s amplitude, discarding displacement directions.
detail.consequence: Matching the descriptor does not recover the full dynamical operator.

notRead: External supplements, raw structures and journal revision; no experiments rerun.

papers.title: Autonomous Agents Coordinating Distributed Discovery Through Emergent Artifact Exchange
papers.summary: Needs, typed artifacts and provenance connect distributed investigations without central task assignment.

representation.rationale: Cross-domain descriptors and explicit provenance enrich represented relations.

transfer.rationale: Resonance mappings yield instantiated FEM-tested designs.

formal.rationale: Typed provenance DAG and gates constrain limited interfaces.

dynamics.rationale: Ribbed lattice variants target frequency bands and modal density.

organization.rationale: Open needs and compatible artifacts route distributed work.

explanation.rationale: Cross-domain relations quantified; shared governing laws unestablished.

validation.rationale: Resonance candidates receive 3D FEM checks, without fabrication.

robustness.rationale: Model comparison and analogy critique; coordination ablations unreviewed.

surprise.observation: Agents construct an executable grammar spanning urban growth and grain evolution.
surprise.boundary: Reduced seven-node similarity does not imply shared mechanisms.

detail.observation: Schema compatibility can be nonempty input-name/payload-key overlap.
detail.consequence: Syntactic compatibility and lineage do not guarantee scientific validity.

notRead: External raw artifacts, supplementary networks and live deployment not audited.

papers.title: GraphAgents: Knowledge Graph–Guided Agentic AI for Cross-Domain Materials Design
papers.summary: A fixed agent sequence explores literature graphs for PFAS-free biomedical-tubing hypotheses.

representation.rationale: Explicit literature relations enrich retrieval and ideation.

transfer.rationale: Graph paths bridge related material-property domains.

formal.rationale: Traversal structure lacks scientific composition guarantees.

dynamics.rationale: Static material requirements dominate this assessed contribution.

organization.rationale: Specialized agents execute a prescribed sequential framework.

explanation.rationale: Generated justifications remain proposed material mechanisms.

validation.rationale: Candidate merits evaluated through generated hypotheses and LLM judging.

robustness.rationale: Five ablations; GPT-5 judging leaves material performance untested.

surprise.observation: Direct graph exploration beats the full pipeline on judged novelty.
surprise.interpretation: Added grounding can trade novelty for evidential context.
surprise.boundary: Judged novelty is not tested materials improvement.

detail.observation: Self-referential and context-poor edges can dominate shortest paths.
detail.consequence: A short relational route can provide weak scientific support.

notRead: Supplementary full agent outputs, raw graphs and code not inspected.
